General.Description:
The north face of Karakal Peak has never been successfully summited. Three expeditions have tried. Two have ended in evacuation, one in death. Experienced alpinist Soren Holt has studied every failed attempt and believes he knows why — and how to succeed where others have not. But reaching the summit of Karakal is only half of his objective. What Soren is really climbing for is the answer to what happened to his father on the same mountain seventeen years ago.

Beyond the Edge is both a technically rigorous mountaineering adventure and a deeply personal story of grief, memory, and the need to understand. Finn Calloway writes about high-altitude climbing with the earned authority of someone who has spent years on rock and ice, conveying with startling precision the physical and psychological reality of existence at extreme altitude — the hallucinations, the moral decisions about who to save and who to leave, the paradox of beauty and mortal danger coexisting in the same panoramic view.

As Soren climbs higher, old secrets surface in fragmentary journal entries, recovered equipment, and conversations with Sherpas who remember a quiet Englishman who climbed alone and did not come back down.

The mountain holds its answer. Getting to it may cost everything.
